name: Borgu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Unclassified Borgu known only from a 2-page wordlist (Meinhof 1917-18); no stress data possible.

sources.citation: Meinhof, Carl. 1915-1916. Sprachstudien im egyptischen Sudan [Vorbemerkung and parts 1-7]. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen VI: 161ff.
sources.note: Series preface (pp. 161-162) states the transcription conventions for accent ('Akzent', 'dynamischen', 'Quantität' tokens) and 'musikalische Töne' that govern how the Borgu forms on p. 196 are marked; needed to interpret the apostrophes/acute marks in the list.

sources.citation: MacMichael, H. A. 1912. The Tribes of Northern and Central Kordofán. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
sources.note: Cited on Meinhof's p. 195 (tokens Mac Michael 1912, Cambridge, Tribes, Northern, Central, Kordofan); may identify the ethnonym 'Borgu' and its region, which bears on the identity note.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record borg1237 and reference record 132549 (Hammarström et al.).
sources.note: Classification 'Unclassifiable', AES extinct, country Sudan, no coordinates; the sole reference is Meinhof 1917-1918 (listed by Glottolog as a minimal description, 2 pp., 'a wordlist or less'). No other descriptive work exists for this languoid.

sources.citation: Hamburg University Press, Afrika und Übersee, 'Vol. 1-92' back-list page.
sources.note: States 'Volumes 1–92 are not yet available in digital form' — the publisher has no open digitization of the 1917/18 volume.

sources.citation: Meinhof, Carl (ed.). 1918-1919. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen Bd. IX (with Sprachstudien im egyptischen Sudan parts 33-44). Univ. of Toronto scan, archive.org afrikaundberse0910meinuoft.
sources.note: Neighbouring volume checked in case Borgu was continued or indexed: the scanned has no occurrence of 'Borgu' (or Borgo/Burgu); the TOC lists Sudan parts 33 Dulman to 44 Bedauye only. Nothing on Borgu.
sources.venue: Univ. of Toronto scan, archive.org afrikaundberse0910meinuoft

sources.citation: Meinhof, Carl. 1917-1918. Sprachstudien im egyptischen Sudan 30: Borgu. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen VIII: 195-196.
sources.note: The only description of the language; full view exists on HathiTrust and Google Books but both block our network. A reader with a browser can open it in seconds: check p. 196 for accent marks on the forms and any footnote on Betonung, and p. 195 for Meinhof's remarks on the informant and the Borku/Teda comparison.

sources.citation: Nachtigal, Gustav. 1879-1889. Saharâ und Sûdân. Berlin/Leipzig (vols. I-III); and Barth, Heinrich. 1862-1866. Sammlung und Bearbeitung central-afrikanischer Vokabularien. Gotha: Perthes.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Both are cited on Meinhof's p. 195 (tokens Nachtigall 1879, Barth 1862, Gotha, Sammlung, Bearbeitung, zentralafrikanischer, Vokabularien) as the comparison material (Teda/Daza, Kanuri, Zaghawa, Borku); relevant only for identity, not for stress.
